question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주어 'he'에 대응하는 과거 시제 동사 'listened'가 올바르게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 주어 'he'가 흥미를 느끼게 된 주체이므로 과거분사 'interested'를 쓰는 것이 어법상 맞습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주어인 'Houser's designs'가 전통에 뿌리를 두고 있는 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 갖는 과거분사 'rooted'가 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 주어 'it'(조각상 Reverie)이 사람들에 의해 감상되는 주체이므로, 조동사 뒤에 수동태 'be appreciated' 형식을 취한 것은 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 구조를 살펴보면, Santa Fe 뒤에서 관계사절이 수식하고 있으며, 뒤따르는 구문 'he worked as a freelance artist'는 주어(he)와 일차적 자동사(worked)를 갖춘 완전한 절입니다. 따라서 관계대명사 (B) which 자리에는 뒤편의 불완전한 자리가 존재하지 않으므로 올 수 없으며, 공간의 부사구 역할을 대신하는 관계부사 where 혹은 전치사를 동반한 in which로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 관계사 — 완전한 절을 이끄는 관계부사 vs 불완전한 절을 이끄는 관계대명사
(C) 분사의 능수동 — 감정을 유발하는지(ing) 느끼는지(ed) 판정
(E) 수동태 — 주어와 동사의 행위 관계(감상되다)로 태 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he __(A) listened__ to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, __(B) which__ he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became __(C) interested__ in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly __(D) rooted__ in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be __(E) appreciated__ by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

passageText: Allan Houser created contemporary Apache sculpture. As a child, he listened to his father's stories about the adventures of Chief Geronimo. This gave him a deep attachment to his ancestral background, an attachment that is shown in his artwork. Houser studied at the Indian School in Santa Fe, New Mexico, and then remained in Santa Fe, where he worked as a freelance artist. During World War II, he traveled to California, where he became interested in the media of sculpture. He created works in a variety of styles and mastered bronze, metal, and stone sculpture. Houser's designs are modern, yet firmly rooted in the special tradition of his Native American forefathers. He drew inspiration from both past and present, but like all successful artists, his sculpture transcends race and language. The sculpture Reverie shows a distinct Native American influence, but it can be appreciated by anyone, regardless of his or her background.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 of의 목적어 자리에 동명사구의 수동형인 being left가 온 것은 어법상 적절합니다. 주어 역할을 하는 행위자가 남겨진 수동의 대상이므로 being p.p. 형태가 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사 other people을 수식하며 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사 who는 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 뒤에 오는 형용사적 성질의 분사 immersed를 수식하는 구조이므로 부사인 similarly가 쓰이는 것이 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 뒤에 주어(everybody), 동사(takes), 목적어(turns)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절이 이어지므로 선행사 a reading group을 수식하는 전치사+관계대명사인 in which의 쓰임은 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 마지막 문장 "Reading a book collaborative is..."에서 주어 역할을 하는 동명사구 'Reading a book'을 수식하는 것은 동사의 성질을 수식하는 부사이어야 합니다. 따라서 형용사 collaborative는 동명사의 준동사적 성질을 수식할 수 없으므로, 명사를 수식하는 형용사가 아닌 부사 collaboratively로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 즉, '책을 협력적으로 읽는 것'이라는 의미 구조를 완성하기 위해서는 부사가 필요합니다.
keyPoints: (E) 형용사 vs 부사 — 준동사인 동명사구를 동작/형태 면에서 수식하기 위해 부사가 필요한 자리 판정
(A) 능동태 vs 수동태 — 남겨지는 대상의 관계를 파악하여 동명사의 수동태 판단
(D) 관계대명사 vs 전치사+관계대명사 — 뒤에 이어지는 절의 구조적 완전성 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: We all enjoy the pleasure of __(A) being left__ alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people __(B) who__ are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else __(C) similarly__ immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group __(D) in which__ everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book __(E) collaborative__ is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

passageText: We all enjoy the pleasure of being left alone with a good book. But sometimes after several hours of immersion we lift our heads and look around, suddenly struck by the quiet, the absence of others. In this situation, we are suffering from reading-induced loneliness. The solution is to read in the company of other people who are reading - whether in a public space such as a café or a library, or in your own home, with your reading friend or partner at the other end of the sofa. Next time you look up, you'll see someone else similarly immersed, and you won't feel alone at all. Reading can be sociable. Consider joining a reading group in which everybody takes turns reading aloud from a novel. Reading a book collaboratively is a wonderful way to share an otherwise internal and solitary experience.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page)

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: They are something useful produced by a mind.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): (A) 전치사구 such as는 뒤에 명사(구)인 software를 취하여 구체적인 예시를 나타내는 정형적 표현으로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): (B) 조건절의 주어 핵이 단수 명사인 ‘a thousand lines of letters in UNIX’에서 핵심 단수 구문(단일 정보 단위 혹은 'a thousand lines'를 단수 취급)으로 수일치되어 단수 정동사 qualifies가 수일치 상 잘 구사되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): (C) something useful이라는 대명사/형용사구를 뒤에서 수식하는 과거분사구로, 그것이 '정신에 의해 생성된' 것이므로 수동 의미의 produced가 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): (D) 명사구 multiple overlapping technologies를 뒤에서 수식하는 형용사구의 핵심 형용사로서, 명사 수식을 담당하는 형용사 자리에 형용사원형인 responsible이 바르게 왔습니다.

question.explanation: (E) "as many an invention"는 어법상 틀린 표현이며 "as much an invention"로 고쳐야 한다. 문장의 뼈대는 'The literary rendering... is as much an invention as the digital rendering...'입니다. 주어가 단수 명사구(The literary rendering)이며 보어로 원급 비교 구문인 'as ~ as'가 사용되었습니다. 이 자리에서 셀 수 없는 정도를 나타내는 부사구 기능을 하면서 명사구 'an invention'을 수식하기 위해서는 원급 부사 'much'를 사용하여 'as much an invention'으로 써야 문장 구조상 옳습니다. 복수 수식에 쓰이는 'many'를 'as many an invention' 형태로 단수 부정관사(an) 앞에 수식어로 두는 것은 비문입니다. 따라서 복수 수식어 형태인 'as many'를 'as much'로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (E) 원급 비교 — 단수 가산명사 앞 정도 부사성 비교 표현으로서의 as much 판단
(B) 주어-동사 수일치 — 주어의 핵심 핵과 동사 간의 수적 일치 판단
(C) 능동태 vs 수동태 — 수식을 받는 대상과 분사의 수동 관계 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, __(A) such as__ software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX __(B) qualifies__ as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful __(C) produced__ by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies __(D) responsible__ for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is __(E) as many an invention__ as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

passageText: We tend to think of technology as shiny tools and gadgets. Even if we acknowledge that technology can exist in disembodied form, such as software, we tend not to include in this category paintings, literature, music, dance, poetry, and the arts in general. But we should. If a thousand lines of letters in UNIX qualifies as a technology (the computer code for a web page), then a thousand lines of letters in English (Hamlet) must qualify as well. They both can change our behavior, alter the course of events, or enable future inventions. A Shakespeare sonnet and a Schubert symphony, then, are in the same category as Google's search engine and the smartphone: They are something useful produced by a mind. We can't separate out the multiple overlapping technologies responsible for a Lord of the Rings movie. The literary rendering of the original novel is as much an invention as the digital rendering of its fantastical creatures. Both are useful works of the human imagination. Both influence audiences powerfully. Both are technological.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime).

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사인 that 뒤에서 과거 시점의 역사적 사실(과거 사바나 시절의 생존)을 서술하므로 과거동사 'kept'를 쓴 것은 시제상 적절하며 주절과 독립된 완결된 정동사 구조를 가집니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 'train + 목적어 + to-v' 구조에서 목적보어 역할을 수행하는 to부정사 구조로, 원형 'train'의 목적격보어로서 'to acknowledge'는 문법적으로 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 'write down'의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌면서, 뒤에 주어가 빠진 불완전한 문장(went well)이 이어지므로 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사이자 명사절을 이끄는 'what'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 'the + 비교급, the + 비교급' 구문에서 조건/양보의 부사절에 해당하는 'the more you appreciate life'의 주어인 'you'에 부합하는 복수형 일반동사 현재 시제 'appreciate'는 수일치상 올바릅니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 전치사 'on'의 목적어 역할을 하는 동시에 뒤에 주어가 없는 불완전한 절('is going wrong')을 이끌어 대명사 지시 관계을 형성하는 관계대명사가 필요합니다. 접속사 'that'은 뒤에 완전한 절을 이끌어야 하므로 이 자리에 올 수 없으며, 앞에 선행사가 없으므로 관계대명사 'that'으로도 쓰일 수 없습니다. 따라서 선행사를 내포하여 '~하는 것'이라는 명사절을 만드는 관계대명사 'what'으로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 관계대명사 vs 접속사 — 선행사 유무와 뒷문장의 완전성 판정
(A) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 수식절 내부에서 과거 사실을 나타내는 정동사 확인
(D) 관계대명사 what — 명사구 목적어 자리에 불완전한 절을 이끄는 격 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that __(A) kept__ us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on __(B) that__'s going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself __(C) to acknowledge__ when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down __(D) what__ went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you __(E) appreciate__ life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

passageText: The human brain is wired to look for threats - a trait that kept us alive when we were living on the savannas but that can prevent happiness in our modern lives. This so-called "negativity bias" can keep you focused on what's going wrong (which explains why complaining is such a popular pastime). To break out of this neural rut, train yourself to acknowledge when things go right. If you keep a calendar or a journal, make a point to write down what went well. If you're more of a verbal processor, start your conversations with friends by sharing a recent win (anything that gives you that yesssss feeling). Where the mind goes, reality follows. The more you appreciate life, the more reasons you have to celebrate it.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 선행사 'shapes, colors, and concepts'를 수식하며 관계절 내에서 learned의 목적어 역할을 하는 목적격 관계대명사로서 'that'의 쓰임은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): recode의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, 뒤에 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절(we see)이 이어지므로 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 'what'은 알맞게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 전치사 역할을 하는 'rather than'의 목적어로서 앞선 'storing'의 의미상 구조와 일치하는 동명사 형태 'storing'은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 동격의 'that'절 내에서 주어인 'our memories'가 재구성되는 행위의 대상이므로, 수동의 의미를 나타내는 과거분사 'reconstructed'는 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 주어는 'People'이며, 'who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail'은 주어를 수식하는 관계사절입니다. 따라서 문장 전체의 정동사인 'struggles'의 진짜 주어는 복수 명사인 'People'이 됩니다. 복수 주어에는 복수 동사를 써야 하므로, 단수 동사 형태인 'struggles'는 비문이며 'struggle'로 고쳐야 어법상 올바릅니다.
keyPoints: (D) 주어-동사 수일치 — 관계사절의 수식을 받는 복수 주어와 복수 동사의 수일치 판단
(B) 관계사 what vs that — 선행사가 없고 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 판단
(E) 분사의 능동 vs 수동 — 의미상 주어인 memories와 '재구성되다'의 수동 관계 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts __(A) that__ we have learned through education. We recode __(B) what__ we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than __(C) storing__ a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail __(D) struggles__ to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are __(E) reconstructed__ through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

passageText: When we see something, we naturally and automatically break it up into shapes, colors, and concepts that we have learned through education. We recode what we see through the lens of everything we know. We reconstruct memories rather than retrieving the video from memory. This is a useful trait. It's a more efficient way to store information - a bit like an optimal image compression algorithm such as JPG, rather than storing a raw bitmap image file. People who lack this ability and remember everything in perfect detail struggle to generalize, learn, and make connections between what they have learned. But representing the world as abstract ideas and features comes at a cost of seeing the world as it is. Instead, we see the world through our assumptions, motivations, and past experiences. The discovery that our memories are reconstructed through abstract representations rather than played back like a movie completely undermined the legal primacy of eyewitness testimony. Seeing is not believing.

markedExpressions.label: (B)

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 문장의 주어 자리에 쓰인 동명사구 'making time for exercise'의 핵 동명사로, 주어 역할을 수행하기에 어법상 올바른 형태입니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 가주어 'it'에 호응하는 s가 붙은 단수 동사 'feels'는 수일치 상 완전히 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 'Whether it's'에서 대명사 'it'에 수일치하는 3인칭 단수 현재형 be동사 'is'가 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 전치사로 기능하는 'rather than' 뒤에서 동명사구 목적어로 쓰인 'viewing'은 문맥과 어법상 모두 자연스럽습니다.

question.explanation: 이 문장은 'That is [명사절]' 구조를 취하고 있습니다. 보어 자리에 온 절의 내부 구조를 보면, 'the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores'가 주어이며 'comes'가 일형식 자동사로 기능하여 주어와 동사(전치사구 into play는 수식어)를 모두 갖춘 완전한 절을 이룹니다. 따라서 관계대명사 'which'는 이 자리에 이끌 명사절이나 부사구의 격(주격 혹은 목적격)을 만족할 수 없어 문장 구조상 비문입니다. 선행사를 포함하면서 뒤에 완전한 절을 이끌 수 있는 관계부사인 'where'로 고쳐 써야 문장 구조상 완전해집니다.
keyPoints: (D) 관계사 — 관계부사 뒤에는 완전한 격 구조의 절이 와야 함
(A) to-v/v-ing — 문장의 주어 기능을 수행하는 동명사구 판단
(C) 수일치 — 가주어 'it'에 상응하는 3인칭 단수 동사 수일치
question.passageWithMarkers: For many of us, __(A) making__ time for exercise __(B) is__ a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often __(C) feels__ like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's __(D) which__ the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than __(E) viewing__ chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

passageText: For many of us, making time for exercise is a continuing challenge. Between work commitments and family obligations, it often feels like there's no room in our packed schedules for a dedicated workout. But what if the workout came to you, right in the midst of your daily routine? That's where the beauty of integrating mini-exercises into household chores comes into play. Let's be realistic; chores are inevitable. Whether it's washing dishes or taking out the trash, these tasks are an essential part of daily life. But rather than viewing chores as purely obligatory activities, why not seize these moments as opportunities for physical activity? For instance, practice squats or engage in some wall push-ups as you wait for your morning kettle to boil. Incorporating quick exercises into your daily chores can improve your health.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 of의 목적어 자리에 동명사구의 명사적 기능을 하는 동명사 형태 noticing이 오는 것은 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 접속사 while 뒤에 주어(it)와 동사(was)를 갖춘 완전한 부사절이 이어져 '~하는 동안에'의 의미를 나타내므로 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 과거진행형 시제(were predicting)를 구성하여 주어인 Your auditory areas가 대상을 예측하고 있었다는 능동적 동작을 자연스럽게 나타내므로 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 주절의 주어(people)의 부수적인 상태나 동작을 설명하는 분사구문으로, 사람들이 '주장하면서'라는 능동의 의미를 지니므로 현재분사 claiming은 적절합니다.

question.explanation: that절의 진짜 주어는 수식어구(of constant background noise, such as...)의 수식을 받는 'a source'로, 단수 명사입니다. 따라서 복수 동사형인 have가 아니라 단수형 동사인 has로 받아야 어법상 올바른 구조가 됩니다. 구체적으로 말해, 'such as' 이하의 예시를 포함하는 전치사구는 주어의 핵심 명사인 source를 수식할 뿐 주어의 수 결정에 영향을 미치지 않기 때문에, 복수형 명사인 noise나 jackhammer, music 등과 무관하게 has를 써야 합니다.
keyPoints: (B) 주어-동사 수일치 — 삽입구나 수식어구가 주어와 동사 사이에 길게 놓일 때 일치시킬 진짜 주어 명사 핵(head)을 찾는 법
(A) 전치사의 목적어 — 명사적 역할을 하는 준동사인 동명사구의 처리
(E) 분사구문의 능동/수동 — 주절의 주어가 행동의 주체일 때 현재분사를 선택하는 태 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: We have all had the experience of suddenly __(A) noticing__ that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, __(B) have__ just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound __(C) while__ it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were __(D) predicting__ its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night __(E) claiming__ that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

passageText: We have all had the experience of suddenly noticing that a source of constant background noise, such as a distant jackhammer or music from a store, has just ceased - yet we hadn't noticed the sound while it was ongoing. Your auditory areas were predicting its continuation, moment after moment, and as long as the noise didn't change you paid it no attention. By ceasing, it violated your prediction and attracted your attention. Here's a historical example. Right after New York City stopped running elevated trains, people called the police in the middle of the night claiming that something woke them up. They tended to call around the time the trains used to run past their apartments.

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is.

markedExpressions.label: (D)

markedExpressions.label: (E)

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): has는 주어인 단수 명사 'The fast pace'에 호응하며, 목적보어로 현재분사구 'piling ~'를 취하는 정동사로 올바르게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): what은 전치사 to의 목적어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이끌며, doing의 목적어가 빠진 불완전한 절을 이끄는 관계대명사로 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): no matter what은 뒤에 불완전한 절을 이끌어 양보의 부사절을 만드는 복합관계대명사 whatever와 같은 역할을 하므로 어법상 옳습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): applies는 단수 명사 주어 'The same'에 동사의 단수형을 수일치시킨 구조로 문법적으로 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 전치사 with 뒤에 '목적어(your phone) + 목적보어(분사)' 구조가 올 때, 목적어와 분사의 관계가 수동인지를 판단해야 합니다. 귀에 대는 동작에 있어서 '전화기'는 귀에 대어지는(눌려지는) 대상이므로 능동의 현재분사 pressing이 아닌, 수동의 과거분사 pressed로 쓰는 것이 맞습니다. 따라서 pressing을 pressed로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 분사의 능동 vs 수동 — 목적어와 분사의 수동 관계 판정
(A) 정동사 vs 준동사 — 주절의 정동사 유무 및 역할 판단
(B) 관계사 what의 격과 쓰임 — 전치사의 목적어절과 수식 관계 분석
question.passageWithMarkers: The fast pace of today's lifestyle __(A) has__ us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to __(B) what__ you're doing at the moment __(C) no matter what__ it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone __(D) pressing__ to your ear. The same __(E) applies__ to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

passageText: The fast pace of today's lifestyle has us piling one thing on top of another. But you should know that multitasking doesn't save any time. Very often, multitasking only slows you down, contrary to popular belief. Give your whole focus to what you're doing at the moment no matter what it is. While doing the laundry, just do the laundry: Listen to the sound of the water as it fills the washing machine and feel the clothes in your hand. It doesn't take up any more time than it would when done with your phone pressed to your ear. The same applies to your work. Focus on one task at a time, and you'll accomplish each task better, and probably faster.

markedExpressions.label: (B)

markedExpressions.label: (C)

markedExpressions.label: (D)

markedExpressions.label: (E)

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 주격 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 단수인 a critical factor이므로 단수 동사인 determines는 수일치상 올바릅니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 'be found + 현재분사(V-ing)' 구문에서 주어인 They(아델리 펭귄들)가 능동적으로 거니는 동작을 취하므로 현재분사 strolling은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 선행사 the leopard seal을 수식하며 주어가 빠진 불완전한 절을 이끄는 주격 관계대명사로서 계속적 용법의 which는 올바르게 사용되었습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(E): 문장의 주어인 One penguin's destiny에 연결되어 술어 역할을 하는 단수 정동사 alters는 어법상 자연스럽습니다.

question.explanation: The moment가 접속사 역할을 하여 '목격되는 순간'을 나타내는 부사절을 이끌고 있으며, 부사절 내의 주어는 앞 문장의 상황(펭귄 한 마리가 포기하고 뛰어드는 것)을 가리키는 지시대명사 that입니다. 지시대명사 that은 3인칭 단수이므로, 복수형 동사 occur가 오면 수일치상 비문이 됩니다. 따라서 단수형 자동사인 occurs로 고쳐야 올바른 문장이 됩니다. 문맥 속에서 'The moment that'을 관계사절의 결합으로 오인하여 복수 명사인 penguins에 수일치시키는 함정에 빠지지 않도록 유의해야 합니다.
keyPoints: (D) 주어-동사 수일치 — 문맥상 단수 지시대명사 주어에 따른 동사의 수 판단
(B) 현재분사 vs 과거분사 — 주어의 능동적 행동을 수식하는 목적보어 성격의 분사 판정
(C) 관계대명사의 계속적 용법 — 선행사 수식과 격의 일치 판정
question.passageWithMarkers: There is a critical factor that __(A) determines__ whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found __(B) strolling__ in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, __(C) which__ likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that __(D) occur__, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny __(E) alters__ the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

passageText: There is a critical factor that determines whether your choice will influence that of others: the visible consequences of the choice. Take the case of the Adélie penguins. They are often found strolling in large groups toward the edge of the water in search of food. Yet danger awaits in the icy-cold water. There is the leopard seal, for one, which likes to have penguins for a meal. What is an Adélie to do? The penguins' solution is to play the waiting game. They wait and wait and wait by the edge of the water until one of them gives up and jumps in. The moment that occurs, the rest of the penguins watch with anticipation to see what happens next. If the pioneer survives, everyone else will follow suit. If it perishes, they'll turn away. One penguin's destiny alters the fate of all the others. Their strategy, you could say, is "learn and live."

question.direction: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

markedExpressions.label: (A)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know.

markedExpressions.label: (B)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs.

markedExpressions.label: (C)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created.

markedExpressions.label: (D)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes.

markedExpressions.label: (E)
markedExpressions.surroundingText: just that it's more ideal not to let yourself falling out of touch in the first place.

wrongOptionExplanations.(A): 전치사 without의 목적어로 동명사인 reaching이 오는 것은 어법상 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(B): 선행사 the distance를 수식하며 관계절 내에서 주어 역할을 하는 주격 관계대명사로서 that은 올바르게 쓰였습니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(C): 주절(We call people ~) 뒤에서 부가적인 상황을 나타내는 분사구문을 이끄는 현재분사 hoping은 적절합니다.
wrongOptionExplanations.(D): 주어인 relationships가 유지되는 대상이므로 수동태인 aren't kept는 형태상 적절합니다.

question.explanation: 문장의 구조를 살펴보면, 사역동사 let이 쓰인 원형부정사 목적격보어 자리를 묻고 있습니다. 'not to let yourself falling'에서 let은 사역동사이고, 목적어인 yourself가 목적격보어 행동인 'fall out of touch'를 행하는 능동의 관계이므로, 현재분사인 falling 대신 원형부정사 fall을 써야 문법적으로 옳습니다. 따라서 falling을 fall로 고쳐야 합니다.
keyPoints: (E) 사역동사의 목적격보어 — 주어와 목적격보어의 능동 관계에 따른 원형부정사 판단
(C) 분사구문의 형태 — 주어와의 능동 관계를 통한 현재분사 선택
(D) 수동태 vs 능동태 — 주어와 동사의 의미적 관계를 통한 태 판단
question.passageWithMarkers: We tend to go long periods of time without __(A) reaching__ out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance __(B) that__ has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, __(C) hoping__ that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships __(D) aren't kept__ up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself __(E) falling__ out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.

passageText: We tend to go long periods of time without reaching out to the people we know. Then, we suddenly take notice of the distance that has formed and we scramble to make repairs. We call people we haven't spoken to in ages, hoping that one small effort will erase the months and years of distance we've created. However, this rarely works: relationships aren't kept up with big one-time fixes. They're kept up with regular maintenance, like a car. In our relationships, we have to make sure that not too much time goes by between oil changes, so to speak. This isn't to say that you shouldn't bother calling someone just because it's been a while since you've spoken; just that it's more ideal not to let yourself fall out of touch in the first place. Consistency always brings better results.
